symptoms.question: Is your fuel level low (near empty)? (yes/no)
Has the car become noticeably slower to accelerate than usual? (yes/no)
Does the engine hesitate or stutter when you accelerate or go uphill? (yes/no)
Do you feel jerking or misfires mainly when accelerating? (yes/no)
Do you see black smoke from the exhaust when accelerating? (yes/no)
Has your fuel consumption increased noticeably recently? (yes/no)
Is the car hard to start when the engine is already warm? (yes/no)
Do you know if the fuel filter has not been replaced for a long time? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Low fuel level with hesitation under load can indicate fuel starvation, especially in corners or on hills.
rules.advice: Avoid running the tank very low and refuel. If the problem remains, have the fuel pick-up and pump checked.

rules.diagnosis: Hesitation and poor acceleration with an old fuel filter suggest restricted fuel flow.
rules.advice: Replacing the fuel filter is a good first step. If symptoms remain, the fuel pump and pressure should be tested.

rules.diagnosis: Black smoke and increased fuel consumption indicate an overly rich mixture or fuel injection issue.
rules.advice: Avoid long drives and have the engine checked soon. Rich running can damage the catalytic converter.

rules.diagnosis: Difficult hot starts with normal fuel level can be caused by fuel vapour or weak fuel pressure.
rules.advice: Mention the hot-start behaviour to a mechanic; checking fuel pressure and injector leakage may be necessary.

rules.diagnosis: Misfire during acceleration with a check engine light suggests injector or mixture problems on one or more cylinders.
rules.advice: Avoid heavy acceleration and have the fault codes read to identify which cylinder is affected.

rules.diagnosis: Black smoke, high fuel consumption and fuel smell with a check engine light strongly suggest a rich-running condition (leaking injectors, incorrect fuel pressure, or faulty airflow/oxygen sensing).
rules.advice: Avoid long drives and have fault codes read. Ask the mechanic to check injector leakage, fuel pressure regulation and airflow/oxygen sensor readings. Rich running can damage the catalytic converter.

rules.diagnosis: Hesitation under load and poor acceleration with an old fuel filter, without black smoke or fuel smell, points to restricted fuel delivery rather than rich-mixture faults.
rules.advice: Replace the fuel filter and have fuel pressure checked. If symptoms remain, test the fuel pump and pressure regulator.
